$doc: The loop's driver — machine-readable on purpose: readiness, batches, and
cap breaches are computed by schedule.mjs, never by eye. Append-mostly:
never delete a ticket; mark it done or decomposed.
status: todo | in-progress | done | blocked | decomposed ('ready' is computed).
files is a CONTRACT: the verifier diffs the branch and fails undeclared
touches (package.json + lockfiles allowlisted for every ticket).
attempts is the durable diagnosis log. evidence holds the INDEPENDENT
re-verify's output, not the builder's claim.
BROWNFIELD NOTE: v0.1 core pre-exists this loop (ledger [0002]). Tickets
S101+ build on it; none may alter src/ semantics (oracle: scope tripwire).
Acceptance sharpened by 2-agent red-team at intake (ledger [0004]).

tickets.title: Story validator: screenshot-based choreography checks for any scrolly HTML file
tickets.context: Read README.md (contract tables), SPEC.md §5 + §14, test/semantics.test.js (puppeteer-core patterns, Chrome path). Build `node test/validate-story.mjs <file.html> [--tier1]` printing a JSON report and exiting 0/1. RED-TEAM-HARDENED DESIGN REQUIREMENTS (non-negotiable): (1) distinctGraphicStates is SCREENSHOT-BASED — at each step's trigger position take a viewport screenshot of the story region and compare hashes; states are distinct only if pixels differ beyond a small threshold. This covers canvas graphics automatically and rejects invisible/occluded attribute toggles. (2) glueTier via RUNTIME INSTRUMENTATION, not text grep: before any page script runs (evaluateOnNewDocument), wrap EventTarget.prototype.addEventListener (flag scroll/wheel/touchstart/touchmove), onwheel/onscroll property setters, window.IntersectionObserver construction, and Element.prototype.getBoundingClientRect; attribute each call to lib vs author via Error().stack correlation with script order — AND the lib script block must be byte-identical to src/scrolly.js (read from disk), else the ENTIRE block counts as author code. tier1 = zero author calls flagged AND author scripts contain only Scrolly.init statement(s) (AST-light check acceptable: strip comments/strings first). tier2 = no flagged calls. else fail, with the specific flagged API named in the report. Words like 'wheel' in comments/strings must NOT trip it. (3) externalUrls: network-request interception is the authority (page.on('request'), anything not file:// on the fixture's own path), plus a secondary source scan matching (https?:)?// in src/href/xlink:href/srcset/CSS url(). (4) consoleErrors: attach console/pageerror/unhandledrejection listeners BEFORE goto; dwell ≥300ms after each scroll position. (5) bidirectionalConsistent: record state (screenshot hash + data-active-step + is-shown set) at each step top-to-bottom, then bottom-to-top, then a NON-MONOTONIC jump order (last→second→last→first); every revisit must match the first visit. (6) Multi-story pages: per-story reports keyed by root index/id; overall exit is the AND of all stories. (7) No fixture-name special-casing: the validator source must not reference fixture filenames. Exit-0 thresholds per story: stepCount>=4, distinctGraphicStates>=4, glueTier ok, no externalUrls, no consoleErrors, bidirectionalConsistent. Craft the broken/clean fixtures named in files (self-contained, lib inlined byte-identical from src/): dead-steps (4 steps, class churn but pixel-identical graphic), external-url (an https:// img AND a protocol-relative //cdn ref), scroll-jack (plain addEventListener('wheel')), scroll-jack-obfuscated (window['addEventListener']('whe'+'el',...) or onwheel= assignment), asymmetric-state (author stepenter draw that accumulates instead of drawing full state — passes everything except bidirectional), runtime-error (author JS throws after load), fetch-external (URL only constructed at runtime via fetch('ht'+'tps://...')), and fixtures-clean/wheel-in-comment (tier-2-clean page whose author script merely CONTAINS the word wheel in a comment — must PASS). test/validator.test.js asserts every contrast pair below, and runs each broken fixture from a COPY at a randomized temp filename (no name sniffing). If this ticket proves bigger than one session, return tooBig with a proposed split (e.g. core driver / instrumentation / fixtures+tests) rather than half-building.
tickets.acceptance:
- `node test/validate-story.mjs index.html` → exit 0, JSON report with all specified fields
- dead-steps → exit 1, report's failure reasons include distinctGraphicStates<4 and do NOT include glueTier/externalUrls failures (exclusivity)
- external-url → exit 1 listing BOTH the https:// and the protocol-relative URL; no other failure reasons
- fetch-external → exit 1 with the intercepted request URL listed (proves real network interception, not source regex)
- scroll-jack AND scroll-jack-obfuscated → exit 1, glueTier=fail naming the flagged API; no other failure reasons
- fixtures-clean/wheel-in-comment → exit 0 (comment/string mentions must not trip instrumentation)
- asymmetric-state → exit 1 solely for bidirectionalConsistent=false
- runtime-error → exit 1 solely for consoleErrors non-empty
- `grep -E 'dead-steps|external-url|scroll-jack|asymmetric|runtime-error|fetch-external' test/validate-story.mjs` → no matches (no fixture sniffing)
- validator.test.js runs every broken fixture via randomized-temp-filename copies and asserts the exact failure reason per case
- `bun test` green

Coordinator gate on merged tree d057805: bun test 45 pass/5 files; validate-story index exit 0; all 7 broken fixtures fail for exactly their one reason (dead-steps:distinctGraphicStates<4, external-url:externalUrls, fetch-external:externalUrls via interception, scroll-jack+obfuscated:glueTier fail naming addEventListener(wheel), asymmetric:bidirectionalConsistent, runtime-error:consoleErrors); clean fixture exit 0; fixture-name grep 0. tickets.title: Chapter timelines: monotonic --progress-<id> variables (geometry + emission)
tickets.context: Read SPEC §15.2 + §5.2 and ARCHITECTURE.md dataflow. tickets.title: data-scrub mechanic: paused-animation scrubbing via structural CSS + init stamp
tickets.context: At init, stamp each [data-scrub] element inside the story once with style --t: var(--progress-<id>) (valueless data-scrub → var(--story-progress)); dangling id → no stamp + one scrolly:-prefixed console.warn (fail-soft; M205 formalizes diagnostics — keep the warn minimal here). destroy() removes stamps. scrolly.css gains the mechanic under .scrolly.is-ready [data-scrub]: animation-duration 1s, play-state paused, fill-mode both, animation-delay calc(var(--t,0) * -1s); under prefers-reduced-motion the delay uses round(var(--t,0)) so scrubs become cuts at the chapter midpoint (SPEC §15.2). CSS stays structural (no typography/color; themes test must stay green). NEW e2e/motion.spec.ts: drive a keyframed element to 0%/~50%/100% of its chapter and assert computed progress advances AND rewinds; reduced-motion emulation yields the quantized value; a page whose lib script is removed still shows the element (no-JS readability §8.1). RED-TEAM: assert data-scrub composes with data-show on the same element (visibility × motion orthogonal), and that author override of animation-delay wins (mechanic is a default, variables are the contract).

tickets.title: Declarative camera: data-camera/data-focus/data-zoom → --camera-transform
tickets.context: Read SPEC §15.3 fully. New src/camera.ts: resolve each focused step's shot — target box in the [data-camera] element's UNTRANSFORMED space (invert current matrix via DOMMatrix/getCTM), data-zoom number or default fit (~70% of stage); root-level data-focus is the establishing shot. Endpoints measured at init/step-change/resize — NEVER per frame. Interpolation in geometry.ts as pure math: pan linear, zoom log-space, across the earlier focused step's chapter progress; unit-test both incl. the k1=k2 and fit cases. story.ts emits one composed --camera-transform on the root; steps without data-focus hold the previous shot; dangling selector → hold + warn; reduced motion → snap to nearer shot (cut). scrolly.css: .scrolly.is-ready [data-camera] { transform: var(--camera-transform, none) } — geometry, so structural. HARD CONSTRAINTS: no scrollTop/scrollTo/scrollBy anywhere (validator instrumentation must stay clean); size bars unchanged — if dist JS would exceed 4KB gz, STOP and escalate (oracle: camera splits to an opt-in file before the bar moves). e2e: mid-chapter screenshot differs from BOTH endpoint screenshots (flight, not cut — anti-gaming: this cannot be satisfied by transition tuning because captures are settle-independent), reverse lands identically, resize re-measures (change viewport, assert new endpoint transform).

tickets.title: data-morph: wrap the atomic step-change writes in View Transitions
tickets.context: With data-morph on the root and document.startViewTransition available, _activate()'s class/attr/is-shown batch runs inside the transition callback. GUARANTEES (each gets an explicit test): stepexit/stepenter fire synchronously in the existing order, never inside/after the transition's promises (semantics.spec.ts event-order assertions must pass UNMODIFIED with data-morph enabled); a new step-change mid-morph calls skipTransition() — latest wins, no queue; progress variables are written outside the wrap every frame; no API / reduced-motion → exact current code path (feature-detect, zero behavior delta). tickets.title: scrolly-director.js: authoring overlay (trigger line, chapter rail, state chip)
tickets.context: New root-level opt-in file (like themes/ — ZERO core diffs; classic script, file://-safe, self-contained). On load: draws the trigger line at viewportHeight × offset for the nearest on-screen story with the offset value labelled (recomputes on resize and per story); a chapter rail listing step ids — click scrolls that step to its trigger (reuse the same math as keyboard.ts; smooth unless reduced-motion); a state chip showing data-active-step, --step-progress/--story-progress and per-chapter --progress-<id> live, plus current is-shown count. Key 'd' toggles everything; input/textarea/contenteditable guarded like keyboard.ts. e2e/director.spec.ts: trigger line's computed position equals innerHeight*offset ±1px for offset 0.5 AND a custom data-offset; rail click activates the right step; toggling off removes every injected node (clean page). RED-TEAM: loading director on a page with zero stories must be a no-op without errors.

tickets.title: Gallery re-cuts on the motion layer (virus flight, scroll-linked scrub, dots-flow morph)
tickets.context: The acceptance test for the whole drive — choreography, not artwork (§14). (1) virus-got-out: replace the hand-rolled [data-active-step] camera transforms with data-camera + per-step data-focus/data-zoom (add invisible anchor elements as shot targets) and move at least the train/flight particles to data-scrub + offset-path keyframes; validator --tier1 PASS; mid-chapter screenshot differs from both endpoints (true scrubbed flight). (2) scroll-linked: delete its progress-event JS; same visual behavior via data-scrub; --tier1 PASS (author JS becomes exactly Scrolly.init). (3) dots-flow: keep the per-step bucket layout in author JS (that is graphic rendering) but delete any positional transition logic; give dots view-transition-name and data-morph on the root; validator PASS at tier2 or better; grep floor: author script contains no 'transition' / manual interpolation. ALL THREE: distinctGraphicStates ≥ the pre-re-cut count (record before/after in evidence); prose and art direction otherwise unchanged — these are re-cuts, not redesigns. Narrative/visual quality remains Jason's gate.
